sentences: `buffer_store_format_*` and `_d16_*` encode every format the loads decode (the same FORMATS table: f32/u32, f16, unorm/snorm 8/16/10-10-10-2, uint/sint 8/16). 1–2-byte elements are merged into their dword with atomic and/or so neighbours are kept.

The atomics use element 0 of the array at the aligned dword address, which also compiles on MoltenVK 1.4.0 (checked with `cs_store` on an Apple M3 Max and Mesa llvmpipe). d16 data is unpacked first (f16 → float for float kinds, 16-bit integers for integer kinds).
Before this, only four f32 formats, rgba16f and rgba8 unorm were stored, and everything else silently stored nothing.
GPU-checked with `runtime/test/shaders/cs_store.asm` (rgba8 unorm, R10G10B10A2 (`2_10_10_10`), two r16f halves of one dword, d16 rgba16f: exact, neighbours untouched).
`buffer_load_format_d16_*` packs pairs the same way.
UNORM/SNORM stores convert NaN to zero before clamping.
On native gfx1036, `buffer_store_format_d16_xyzw` into RGBA8_UNORM/SNORM matched clamp, scale by 255/127 and round to nearest even for all 63,488 finite binary16 encodings.
Both infinities saturated and all 2,046 NaNs stored zero in both wave32 and wave64.
The translated sweep matched all 65,536 bytes per format on RTX 5080 and Radeon Graphics.
For normalized stores with format 56 (8/8/8/8) or 50 (10/10/10/2), a Z,Y,X,W descriptor exchanges the red and blue memory fields after filling absent input components with zero.
Native gfx1036 confirmed both channel orders at all four instruction widths for packed and ordinary stores in wave32 and wave64.

A store with fewer components than its format writes the whole element, with 0 for the components it doesn't give (`_xy` into 32_32_32_32 leaves z = w = 0, `_xyz` into 16_16_16_16 leaves w = 0); into a one-channel format only x is written.
Measured natively on a Radeon 680M (gfx1035, RDNA2), and GPU-checked by `cs_fmt_xy_xyz.asm` for 32_32_32_32, 16_16_16_16, 8_8_8_8 UNORM and UINT and 32 (TEST-185).
Unsigned integer stores saturate to the destination channel width.
On native gfx1036, RGBA8_UINT, RG16_UINT and RGBA16_UINT clipped overflowing inputs to 255 or 65535, with RGBA32_UINT as a full-width control.

For normalized stores with format 56 (8/8/8/8) or 50 (10/10/10/2), a Z,Y,X,W descriptor exchanges the red and blue memory fields after filling absent input components with zero; native gfx1036 confirmed both channel orders at all four instruction widths for packed and ordinary stores in wave32 and wave64.

`tbuffer_store_format_*` is not translated. 8- and 16-bit SINT stores clamp the signed 32-bit value to [-2^(w-1), 2^(w-1) - 1] (300 stores 127 into 8_SINT, -129 stores -128), and the 8/16-bit UINT formats 5, 11 and 18 saturate like the others; measured natively on gfx1036 for x, xy, xyzw and d16_xyzw stores (a d16 half is read as a signed 16-bit integer for SINT, so 0xff80 stores -128) with the runtime's selectors (X001, XY01, XYZW) and checked by `tests/semantic/test_buffer_format_narrow_int.py` (until 2026-11-22 those formats stored nothing).

`tbuffer_store_format_*` and its `_d16_*` forms take the instruction's format instead of the V#'s, as the tbuffer loads do: only that format is encoded, and its element size decides the bounds check (an 8_UNORM byte is stored where the V#'s 16-byte element would not fit; a 16-byte element is dropped where the V#'s 4-byte one would fit).
A V# whose FORMAT is 0 (INVALID) still disables the store.
No `format:` modifier is GFX10's default, BUF_FMT_8_UNORM; a format FORMATS has no encoder for stays `Unsupported`.

Measured natively on a Radeon 680M (gfx1035, wave32 = wave64) and GPU-checked by `cs_tbuffer_store.asm` (13 stores: f32, f16, 8_8_8_8 UINT and UNORM, 2_10_10_10, d16, the default format, more and fewer components than the format has, both bounds cases, a V# with FORMAT 0; exact on an RTX 3050 and the 680M); CPU-checked by `tests/semantic/test_tbuffer_store.py`.
